clue.text: Any old guy would fall for her!

definitions.text: Any old guy would fall for her

indicators.note: to fall here is to tumble into disorder, so the letters of the three words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman so charming that every man around falls for her.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds the answer: 'would fall' rearranges ANY OLD GUY, and such a woman is just the sort any man would fall for.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretty girl is the classic object of every man's affection in the clue's picture.

clue.text: After performance on stage take note for work

parts.note: an opera is a sung performance on stage
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A singer is told to take a note after the show, as a matter of work.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or work, as a machine does.

clue.text: Starting to develop nylons, initially with a perfume

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word nylons beside it

parts.note: a scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: A woman in nylons and a dab of perfume is just beginning to bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent describes something just coming into being, in its earliest stage of growth.

clue.text: Young creatures that always need permits to go outside

indicators.note: the word for permits must go outside, wrapping round the word for always

parts.note: lets means permits or allows
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: Animals that forever need a permit before they can go out.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverets are hares in their first year, so they are young animals.

clue.text: Showed boredom — going over study method

indicators.note: going over suggests turning back the whole run of pieces, so they are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a den is a private study or room
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: A student is bored by revising a method of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' turns DENWAY round as a whole, giving YAWNED.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawn is the familiar physical sign of tedium, so yawning displays a lack of interest.

clue.text: Frenchman who beat rap on fraud

indicators.note: a fraud is a fake, so the letters of beat rap on are a counterfeit arrangement to be put right

explanation.surface: A Frenchman escaped a criminal charge relating to fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat rap' looks like dodging a criminal charge, but it is anagram material with 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was the French emperor, the most famous Frenchman of his era.

clue.text: Almost essential, and almost belonging to me like a, B or c

indicators.note: almost means the word for essential falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: vital means essential

indicators.note: the second almost again drops the final letter, this time from the word for belonging to me

parts.note: mine means belonging to me

explanation.surface: Something nearly essential and nearly one's own, compared with letters of the alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: VITA(L) plus MIN(E). The definition uses the letters A, B and C as examples of nutrients; the capitals are scrambled to hide that.
explanation.definitionFit: A, B and C are well-known examples of these dietary nutrients, so they define by example.

clue.text: Wild rose in elegant setting

indicators.note: setting suggests the letters of in and elegant are arranged afresh, as a jeweller sets stones

explanation.surface: A wild rose looks lovely in an elegant setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' reads as a backdrop, but it rearranges IN plus ELEGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a species of wild rose with fragrant leaves.

clue.text: Declaring, when a victory is due

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for victory, as in V-sign
owing means due to be paid

explanation.surface: Someone announces that a victory is now deserved.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to state openly, so avowing means asserting or proclaiming.

clue.text: Thoughtful writer given heart

annotationWithheld.why: Thoughtful writer given heart (7): PEN for writer leaves SIVE unaccounted for; 'given heart' supplies no such letters, so the clue appears cut short and no search found the full text

clue.text: Falls again, disastrously, for artist

indicators.note: disastrously suggests the word again comes to grief and its letters are scrambled

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist suffers another disastrous tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrously' makes NIAGA from AGAIN; RA is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the US-Canada border, so it names falls.

clue.text: Arrived with nothing, and given bread, say for a short appearance

parts.note: came means arrived
O is the round figure zero, nothing

indicators.note: say signals that the word for bread is pronounced, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: Someone turns up empty-handed, is handed bread and has a brief walk-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a small but notable part played by a well-known actor in a film or play.

clue.text: Ties up to get sail fixed

indicators.note: fixed suggests the letters of get sail are repaired or rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors tie up the rigging so as to get the sail secured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' looks like securing the sail, but it rearranges GET SAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To ligate is to tie off or bind, especially a blood vessel in surgery.

clue.text: Romantic notion precedes tip

indicators.note: precedes means the word for notion comes before the word for tip

parts.note: an idea is a notion
to list is to tip or lean over, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A dreamy idea comes ahead of a useful tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic in the sense of a visionary is someone who pursues lofty ideals over realities.

clue.text: Group that sued patient, given odd letters

indicators.note: odd letters means the first, third, fifth and so on are taken from sued patient

explanation.surface: A band that took a hospital patient to court, given strange letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking letters one, three, five and so on from SUED PATIENT gives S, E, P, T, E, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A septet is a set of seven, especially seven musicians playing together.

clue.text: High room — mistrust, acoustically?

parts.note: space means room, as in 'room to move'

indicators.note: acoustically signals that the word for mistrust is taken as it sounds, not as spelt

parts.note: doubt is mistrust

explanation.surface: Distrust of a lofty room with odd acoustics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acoustically' works because the B in the word for mistrust is silent, so the sound needs no B; 'High' means intoxicated, not tall.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaced out is slang for dazed or intoxicated, as if on drugs.

clue.text: Creature that might have them raw or cooked

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of them raw or are doctored, as cooked books are rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal you might eat either raw or cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks culinary but rearranges THEM RAW OR.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthworm is a burrowing invertebrate living in soil.

clue.text: Attack — when sailor is speaking

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: is speaking indicates the word for sailor is heard rather than read

parts.note: a salt, or old salt, is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor speaks while launching an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent onslaught on a person or position.

clue.text: Situation of fool, protecting one cat in the lead

indicators.note: protecting means the word for fool surrounds and guards the other pieces

parts.note: a loon is a fool or crazy person

indicators.note: in the lead means the cat goes in front of the one

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An idiot guards a lone cat on a leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the lead' sounds like a dog on a leash, but it orders the two pieces inside, with the animal ahead of the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A location is a place or position, where something is situated.

clue.text: One who plays music to fish first

parts.note: a bass is a fish
1st, read as IST, is first

explanation.surface: An angler serenades fish before starting.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure 1 in '1st' is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassist is a bass guitarist or double bass player in a band.

clue.text: Works for nothing, performing revue

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters of revue are put through their paces in a new order

explanation.surface: Actors work for free in a revue.
explanation.definitionFit: An oeuvre is the whole body of work produced by an artist or writer.

clue.text: Oblivious of girl at Hertfordshire town

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
Ware is a market town in Hertfordshire, a county just north of London

explanation.surface: A girl in a Hertfordshire town has no idea what's happening.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unaware is lacking any knowledge or consciousness of something.

clue.text: Profligate needs to shelter money as a matter of course

indicators.note: to shelter means the word for profligate wraps around the word for money

parts.note: a roue is a debauched, profligate man
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A wastrel naturally needs to hide his money.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a regular procedure, something done habitually.

clue.text: Discipline is found in celibate

indicators.note: found in means the word is sits inside the word for celibate

parts.note: chaste means abstaining from sex, celibate

explanation.surface: Self-discipline is a quality of the celibate.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to rebuke or punish someone severely.

clue.text: Bands sometimes seen in windows

explanation.surface: Ribbons occasionally displayed in shop windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Sashes are bands of cloth worn round the waist or shoulder; they are also the sliding frames of a sash window.

clue.text: When even America protects silver plant

parts.note: as means when

indicators.note: protects means the pieces for even and America surround the symbol for silver

parts.note: par means even or equal
US is short for United States
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Even America guards its silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a vegetable plant whose young shoots are eaten.

clue.text: Denies any connection with pig noises outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for noises goes round the word for pig

parts.note: dins are loud noises
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: Someone denies being responsible for pigs making noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Disowning is refusing to acknowledge or accept responsibility for someone or something.

clue.text: Twitch, potting one brown — great!

indicators.note: potting means the word for twitch takes the other pieces in, as a pot holds something

parts.note: a tic is a nervous twitch
I is the Roman numeral for one
tan is light brown

explanation.surface: A snooker player twitches while potting the brown ball - great shot!
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker the brown is one of the coloured balls; 'potting' is the insertion here.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means huge, as of the mythical giants called Titans.

clue.text: Swelling increases itchiness?

parts.note: ups means increases, as in 'ups the price'
an itch is a craving, so itchiness is an urge

explanation.surface: A rash that grows ever more itchy.
explanation.definitionFit: An upsurge is a sudden rise in something, a swell.

clue.text: Strolled with relative on Sunday — and shot deer!

indicators.note: on means the relative comes after the day in an across answer

parts.note: an aunt is a relative

indicators.note: shot suggests the letters of deer are blasted into a new order

explanation.surface: A Sunday walk with an aunt ends with a deer being shot.
explanation.definitionFit: To saunter is to walk in a slow, relaxed manner.
